design_rationale:
WORKLOG task 0 (net_energy_metering, category nem). Current as of rework round 2.
[Step 0 draw] draw_counts.py --task 0 -> {"prerequisite_problems": 2, "problems": 3, "factor_counts": [5, 4, 6]}; revaluation 4 factors, estimated export credit 5, move-out termination 6.
[Scope snapshot] Claimed: nem_ext_export_credit_revaluation (revalue_export_credit_a4b62fb5, agent), nem_ext_estimated_export_credit (book_estimated_export_credit_93ce1e35, agent), nem_ext_move_out_termination (end_net_metering_at_move_out_41499158, user). Task 1 holds the anniversary family (expiry, cash-out) and the requested termination; scopes disjoint, union = 6 policies.
[Base write-surface note / route-around] Base nem_application_fee, nem_grid_access_charge and nem_credit_application trigger unconditionally into service tables, and nem_application triggers the fee, so no task tool may write them; withdrawal and termination are the only customer-owned events. The difficulty lives on export-credit entries (revaluation, estimated booking), settlements by check, forfeitures and terminations. The termination tool records the cash-out payout and the surrendered remainder in the same termination event so the bank ends at zero.
[Design thesis] Surface goal: end the solar agreement at the house the customer moved out of and be paid what is left. Scored root: the move-out payout. Hidden chain: the final period (estimated read) has no export credit, and the estimate is valued at the rates of the preceding credit, which was booked at winter rates on a summer bill. Chain revaluation -> estimate -> move-out; both edges value_input. Breadth: Schedule RT seasonal/TOU rates and PSCR, bill seasons, read types, bill kinds and billed kWh, the closed hosting agreement and the active Grand Haven agreement (service), 12-month ledger totals (nem), tenure since PTO (date).
[Problem-tree card] Root nem_ext_move_out_termination (user). Edge move_out -> estimated_export_credit: value_input u_bank, state form, 'The move-out settlement is not fixed until every billing period billed on the hosting service agreement since permission to operate has an export credit in the net metering history.' (negated direction). Only the estimated booking creates an export credit for a period without one. False at opening: final bill 2026-10-20 (period 2026-09-18..2026-10-16, estimated) has no export credit; latest credit ends 2026-09-17. Edge estimated -> revaluation: value_input ye_rate_on, state form, 'The estimated export credit is fixed only after the most recent export credit in the net metering history carries the per-kWh rates that the revaluation of export credits fixes for it.' (affirmative). Only the revaluation rewrites recorded rates. False at opening: the 2026-09-17 entry records 0.17658/0.09332 (winter) on a summer bill. Order: revaluation (step 8), estimate (10), termination (12). Deletion runs: skip 8 -> estimate 44.77, payout 140.39; skip 10 -> payout 109.85, surrender 34.48. Persona names no prerequisite; tools validate none.
[Base-invariant card] Revaluation and estimate (nem_export_credit): nem_export_credit_calculation.credit_operating_only (status operating, correlated by nem_agreement_id); nem_program_interactions policy scope (communicating bidirectional meter, no battery, no budget plan). Move-out: nem_true_up_rule.settle_once (operating, no earlier termination settlement); nem_modification_transfer_termination policy scope (no buyer or other customer has started service at the address). No time gate applies. The final bill is dated 2026-10-20, outside true-up month 03, so the move-out rule's scope holds, and the payout 150.40 is at least the 25.00 check minimum.
[Business-object card] Agreement 635839c4-a55b-40f0-a3c4-13fad75da453. Revaluation object: the latest export credit (2026-09-17), whose bill is an actual read. Estimate object: the final bill's period, keyed by billing_period_end 2026-10-16. Settlement object: the recorded bank after both writes. 12-month windows: ledger rows with billing_period_end in the 12 whole months before 2026-10-23 (2025-11-17..2026-10-16); bills dated 2025-11-20..2026-10-20.
[Factor card] Revaluation (4): seasonal_energy_rates (summer TOU 0.27940/0.11573; winter baseline 70.02), time_of_use_split method (recorded 118/527; all off-peak 61.99), supply_cost_component (residential less-NBC rider 0.00253; the aggregated business rider's 'nothing added' 79.67), non_bypassable_charge_phase_in (54 months, full 0.02215; none 95.59); all at baseline 72.85; result 81.30. Estimate (5): estimate_basis method (final bill -> 645 x 0.9355 = 603.3975; unscaled 54.94), daylight_shift 0.72 (71.25), vacancy_uplift 1.05 (final bill 470 kWh vs 350; 48.92), provisional_estimate_factor 0.92 (one other estimate, 2026-01-20; 55.77; near-miss: the 2025-10-20 estimate is 12 whole months back, counting it would give 0.85), estimated_on_peak_share 0.16 (40.37); all at baseline 61.99; result 51.33 (67/353 kWh). Move-out (6): offsettable_charge_average method 67.70 over 11 regular bills (148.93; near-miss: the 2025-10-20 bill is outside, the final bill is not regular), full_value_months 1.0 (138.55), tenure_months 0.5 (138.55), surplus_share 0.55 (192.75; near-miss: the 2025-10-17 period is outside the window), staying_uplift 0.10 (140.99), estimated_read_holdback 0.24 on the final estimated bill (162.72); all at baseline 195.66; result 150.40, surrender 45.26.
[Seed] Customer; closed Holland Schedule RT agreement (non-electric heat, stopped 2026-10-16, balance 13.50); active Grand Haven agreement; AMI Bidirectional Net Meter at Holland; NEM-R agreement (PTO 2022-03-16, true-up month 03, bank 133.05); 19 bills 2025-04..2026-10 (estimated reads 2025-10-20, 2026-01-20 and the final bill); 18 export credits and 19 credit applications. Summer-2025 inverter outage explains the low July/August 2025 credits. The 2026-09-17 credit is the mis-rated object; every other export credit follows the revaluation rule's rates for its season, and every application equals the lesser of the bank and the bill's energy plus PSCR charges. Both March true-up bills found a zero bank, so no settlement was owed.
[Persona] Delphine, teacher on lunch break; volunteers only move-out, empty house for sale, ending the agreement and being paid; phone on locate, SSN last four + ZIP on verify (email only if a third detail is asked); new address only when asked; a generic passive consent if the agent says something must be done first; runs the hand-over tool with figures as given; closes on 'terminated'.
[Verification run] Authoring evaluator replaying gold with the real tools: revaluation 81.30 (bank 133.05 -> 144.33); estimate 51.33 (-> 195.66); move-out 150.40 / 45.26 (-> 0.00). Applying the revaluation rule to the banked estimate returns its recorded 51.33 (no change). Gate results are listed in the round-2 log below.
[Revisions round 1] surplus_share tied to the 12-month export vs applied comparison; limit months reduced; LATEST kWh reads changed to SUM over the period; summer-2025 outage seeded; empty FKs -> null; unread rows dropped.
[Revisions round 2 - policy audit] F1: the revaluation rule now never revalues a credit whose bill was an estimated read (its revalued amount is the recorded amount; compute guard xr_recorded), so the banked estimate is no second object. F2: the supply-cost fall-through is now the aggregated business rider (in scope). F3: estimate_basis replaces billing_day_scaling (final bill prorate / regular bill after an estimated preceding read: 3-month average / otherwise carry over). F4: vacancy keyed on the final bill's billed kWh against the preceding bill. F5: provisional keyed on other estimated bills; 2026-01-20 seeded as estimated. F6: holdback keyed on final vs regular estimated bill; share 0.24 (also removes the half-cent tie behind T0-O1). O1/O3/O4/O5: check-minimum, forfeit-rider and true-up-month scope sentences added; staying uplift requires the hosting agreement to be closed. O2: split overrides declared. U1: move-out tool renamed with a fresh uuid8 (41499158). Persona consent line made generic.
[Draft recomputation from visible context] Latest credit has winter rates on a summer actual-read bill -> revalue 81.30; final period lacks a credit -> 645 x 0.9355 x 0.72 x 1.05 x 0.92 = 420 kWh -> 67/353 at the revalued rates -> 51.33; settlement 150.40 paid, 45.26 surrendered. Agrees with gold.
[Round 2 gate re-run] EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK (closure 61 = initial 61), SOLVABILITY OK, COMPUTE OK, GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.
[Round 2 accepted observations] O6: a billed period with an actual read always receives its export credit at billing, so only estimated-read periods can lack one and the move-out sentence always resolves to the estimated booking; no rule change. O7: the base sentences on the sale-time bank settlement and the return to a communicating meter ground no edge of either tree; the base is frozen and neither tree rests on them.
user_scenario: You are Delphine Arceneaux, a 47-year-old middle-school science teacher calling on your lunch break, friendly but a little rushed, speaking in short sentences. You moved out of your house at 418 Pinecrest Drive, Holland, MI 49424 on October 16, 2026, and the electric service there has already been stopped. The house has rooftop solar on a net metering agreement with Lakeshore. The house is empty and listed for sale; nobody has bought it and nobody has started service there. You open by saying: "I moved out of my Holland house and I want to end the solar net metering agreement there and have whatever credit is left on it paid out to me." You do not know any account or agreement numbers. When the agent asks how to find your account you give your phone number, 6164501837. When the agent asks you to verify who you are, you give the last four digits of your Social Security number, 7642, and your billing ZIP code, 49417; only if the agent says one more detail is needed do you add your email, delphine.arceneaux@lakemail.net. If the agent asks about your new home, you say service there already started at 77 Lakeview Terrace, Grand Haven, MI 49417, which is now your mailing address too. You have no idea how the solar credits are worked out and you offer no figures or opinions about them. If the agent tells you something needs to be done on the Holland account before the agreement can be closed out, you say that is fine and to go ahead. When the agent tells you how much will be paid to you and how much of the credit will not be paid, you accept it without arguing. Ending the agreement is your own decision, so when the agent hands you the step to end it, you carry it out yourself using the agreement number and the two amounts exactly as the agent gave them to you. Once you see that the agreement is terminated, you thank the agent and end the call.

request_binding.action_semantics: A banked export credit whose recorded rates are not the rates the revaluation rule fixes is a state-owed correction on the agreement the customer is closing; it is not a new credit (the period already has one) and not a settlement.

discriminator.business_meaning: export credit already banked at rates other than the revalued rates

stage_provenance.fact: The revaluation is a synchronous correction of an existing ledger entry; the period's actual read and kWh already stand in the records.

base_preconditions.condition: Export credits are banked only for an agreement in operating status, and energy exported from a battery charged from the grid earns no credit where storage_grid_charging_export_allowed is false.

The interactions policy (opt-out meter exclusion, battery dispatch export credit, budget billing) governs export credits; the agreement holds a communicating AMI Bidirectional Net Meter and no battery or budget plan.

request_binding.action_semantics: Each billing period of an operating agreement banks one export credit; the final bill's period has none, so an estimated credit is owed. It is a new entry for a period without one, unlike the revaluation of an existing entry.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.nem_agreement_id: Value 635839c4-a55b-40f0-a3c4-13fad75da453. Basis: the find_nem_agreements return for the customer lists exactly one agreement, the operating Rider NEM-R agreement at the Holland service agreement; the docstring says 'reference number of the net metering agreement ... that owns the entry'. Uniqueness: it is the only agreement the customer holds and the owner of the entry revalued.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.nem_ledger_id: Value 43e0c33f-f967-409c-b3dd-068fda7e21cc. Basis: the rule 'This rule governs the revaluation of the most recent export credit banked under an agreement whose rider values exports at a retail rate'; the find_nem_ledger return shows the export credit with the latest billing_period_end 2026-09-17 is this entry, and its recorded rates 0.17658/0.09332 are the winter rates while the bill for that period (2026-09-20) is a summer bill. Uniqueness: no later export credit exists at handling time (the final period has none yet), so any correct agent selects this entry.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.credit_rate_on_peak: 0.25978 = summer on-peak energy rate 0.27940 (bill season summer AND Schedule RT has on-peak hours) + supply-cost component 0.00253 (Power Supply Cost Recovery 0.00421 x successor share 0.60, rounded to five decimals, retail-less-NBC basis) - non-bypassable charge 0.02215 in full (54 whole months from permission to operate 2022-03-16 to 2026-09-17, at least 24), rounded to five decimals; the binding xr_rate_on of the policy compute.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.credit_rate_off_peak: 0.09611 = summer off-peak energy rate 0.11573 + 0.00253 - 0.02215, rounded to five decimals; binding xr_rate_off.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.revalued_credit_usd: 81.30 = 118 on-peak kWh x 0.25978 + 527 off-peak kWh x 0.09611 = 30.65404 + 50.64997 = 81.30401, rounded to the cent once. Factors: seasonal energy rates (summer TOU tier; winter baseline gives 70.02), time-of-use split (recorded split because the 2026-09-20 bill is an actual read on a TOU schedule; all-off-peak baseline gives 61.99), supply-cost component (successor share; none gives 79.67), non-bypassable charge (full; none gives 95.59).

evaluation_criteria.objective: Unlock the estimated export credit tool.
evaluation_criteria.necessity: First half of the unlock/call pair; no DB effect.

edges.condition: Every service_bills row of the hosting service agreement with billing_period_end after the permission to operate date has a nem_export_credit row with the same billing_period_end, and credit_bank_balance includes it.
edges.policy_source: The move-out settlement is not fixed until every billing period billed on the hosting service agreement since permission to operate has an export credit in the net metering history.

edges.condition: The most recent nem_export_credit row of the agreement records credit_rate_on_peak and credit_rate_off_peak equal to the revalued rates of the export credit revaluation rule.
edges.policy_source: The estimated export credit is fixed only after the most recent export credit in the net metering history carries the per-kWh rates that the revaluation of export credits fixes for it.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain, so the topological order is unique: the revaluation targets the most recent export credit, which is the 2026-09-17 entry only before the estimated credit is banked; the estimate reads the revalued rates; the move-out settles the bank after both. Once the estimate is banked it becomes the most recent export credit, but the revaluation rule never revalues a credit whose bill was an estimated read (its revalued amount is its recorded 51.33), so no further write follows. Booking the estimate first would value it at the winter rates (44.77).

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping step 10: bank 144.33 instead of 195.66, the holdback reads the 81.30 entry (19.51), payout_usd 109.85 instead of 150.40 and surrendered 34.48 instead of 45.26; the 2026-10-16 export credit row is missing from the terminal state.

Skipping step 8: the estimate values 67/353 kWh at 0.17658/0.09332, estimated_credit_usd 44.77 instead of 51.33, and the move-out payout becomes 140.39 (surrender 37.43); the 2026-09-17 entry keeps 70.02.
